question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x-3y=1 \\ 5x+4y-2z=0 \\ y-z=3\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-21,$ then $y=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+(-3)y+0z=1 \\ 5x+4y+(-2)z=0 \\ 0x+1y+(-1)z=3\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=-21\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{y},$ we take the coefficients matrix, replace the second column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(0+6)-(-5-0)+0 \\  & =18+5 \\  & =23.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{23}{-21}=-\frac{23}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$
